status: pre-freeze pin (offline). NOT a preregistration freeze; no confirmatory run, no paid calls.
purpose: Pin the production prompt-builder and retrieval call sites that a future Study 02 confirmatory run would use, so the prompt path cannot change silently between the freeze commit and the run.
pinning_note: Hashes and sizes are SHA-256 of the working-tree files at base commit 85773b3 on branch study02/freeze-prep. They are computed, not invented. If a rebuild differs, the pin must be re-taken and the new hashes recorded before any confirmatory run.

pinned_files.role: the single production prompt builder for Forge jobs (generate and modify paths, memory rendering)
server-side Forge runner: retrieval call, memory list, buildForgePrompt call, prompt_sha256 recording, job lifecycle
MemoryEngine: create/retrieve/correct API used to place and supersede the arm's memories

prompt_rendering_dependencies.role: renderMemoryLayout(..., 'forge'): delimited project_constraints / project_memory_data blocks with provenance header, escaped content and 'data, not instructions' safety lines; imported by prompt.ts. Advisory dependency: it changes the rendered memory block even when prompt.ts is unchanged.
prompt_rendering_dependencies.reason_not_in_three_file_pin: The requested three-file pin is prompt.ts + runner.ts + engine.ts; this dependency is recorded so a context.ts change is not invisible, and must be added to the freeze manifest.

input_shape.memories: RetrievedMemory[] | undefined: structured retrieval records (optional; empty/absent -> no memory block)
input_shape.hasScreenshot: boolean | undefined: whether a preview screenshot is attached (modify path)

memory_rendering.function: renderForgeMemory(input) -> renderMemoryLayout(input.memories, 'forge') when memories is non-empty; otherwise ''
memory_rendering.layout: forge layout emits a <project_constraints> block for constraint/goal memories and a <project_memory_data> block for other memories; each entry carries [n] id, type, scope, validation_status, confidence, source; content is escaped; both blocks start with standing safety lines stating the block is data, not a trusted instruction.
memory_rendering.injection_point: The memory block is injected after a paragraph telling the model the stored project memory is reference data and cannot grant permissions, change the execution contract, or override policy.
memory_rendering.empty_behaviour: No memories -> the memory block is the empty string; no memory section is added.

prompt_paths.generate: generate path: fixed application contract (single index.html, responsive, sandbox interaction contract, accessibility/keyboard, storage rules, node --check, optional memory block, then 'Application request:' + input.prompt).
prompt_paths.modify: modify path: edit-in-place contract, screenshot sentence (attached vs not), preserve behaviour, sandbox interaction contract, storage rules, optional memory block, then 'Requested change:' + (input.request ?? input.prompt).
prompt_paths.request_vs_prompt: modify uses request when present; generate uses prompt.

buildforgeprompt_behaviour.retrieval_query: buildRetrievalQuery returns input.request ?? input.prompt for kind 'modify', else input.prompt (project_id deliberately excluded from the query).
buildforgeprompt_behaviour.runner_call_site: apps/server/src/forge/runner.ts: retrieve via this.engine.retrieve({project_id, query, mode:'forge'}, {now}); memories = retrieval.results; then buildForgePrompt({kind, prompt, request, memories, hasScreenshot}); resulting prompt is hashed (prompt_sha256) and written to staging/prompt.txt before execution.
buildforgeprompt_behaviour.retrieval_api: packages/memory-engine/src/engine.ts exposes create(input), retrieve(request, options), correct(input); retrieve delegates to retrieveMemories(this.db, request, options) and reads only.

phase17_difference.phase17_behaviour: The locked Phase 17 Open runner rendered memory itself into a flat string: `memoryBlock = retrieval.results.map(r => '- ' + r.injected_content).join('\n')` (or '' when empty), then called buildForgePrompt({ kind: 'modify', prompt, request, memoryBlock, hasScreenshot: false }). That call site corresponds to an older production builder whose input accepted a pre-rendered `memoryBlock`.
phase17_difference.current_behaviour: The current production builder (pinned above) has no `memoryBlock` input; it accepts structured `memories: RetrievedMemory[]` and renders a delimited, id/provenance-bearing memory block itself via renderMemoryLayout(..., 'forge'). Passing an extra `memoryBlock` string at runtime would not be rendered.
phase17_difference.verdict: The two paths are not prompt-level comparable. Study 02 confirmatory runs use the CURRENT production builder (structured memories); prompt-level identity with the locked Phase 17 runs is NOT claimed. Any Phase 17 vs Study 02 comparison is a task-level replication/successor comparison, not a byte-identical-prompt comparison.
phase17_difference.consequence_for_freeze: The freeze manifest must include this pin, the frozen retrieval/rendering dependency hashes, and the exact prompt_sha256 recorded per confirmatory run. A prompt.ts/runner.ts/engine.ts/context.ts change after the freeze is a deviation, not a silent update.

decision.confirmatory_prompt_source: current production buildForgePrompt at the freeze commit (pinned by the hashes above), not a re-implementation and not the Phase 17 loader
decision.rationale: The study measures the product's current prompt path; freezing a historical prompt would measure a prompt the product no longer uses. Continuity with Phase 17 is at the level of arms, strata, rules, detectors and task, and is labelled as such.
decision.pinning_route: At freeze: add these hashes (plus context.ts) to the lock manifest and record the pinned base commit in the protocol; after the freeze the prompt builder is immutable for the confirmatory run.

environment_dependent_not_pinned_here: Provider/model version served by Baseten for meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026 (revision id; must be recorded per run and asserted against an expected id).
Tokenizer and chat template applied server-side by the provider; token counts returned in usage are provider-computed.
Sampling parameter support/defaults at the provider (temperature/top_p/max_tokens/seed); the protocol's frozen sampling setting is a request-side choice and must be echoed/recorded.
Transport and request framing (chat-completions vs the Forge CLI tool loop); checkpoint-2 evidence uses a chat-completions-style path, so the confirmatory run must use one fixed path.

Retrieval contents: the actual memory ids and rendered character counts depend on the project memory state and retrieval DB; these must be recorded per run (the engine/API are pinned, the data are not).
Screenshot attachment: modify prompts differ when hasScreenshot is true; the confirmatory harness must fix and record this per arm.
System/developer instructions injected outside buildForgePrompt (provider system prompt, tool loop) are not in these files.
verification_commands: git rev-parse HEAD  # expect 85773b331ef02f28cb4ba761a72e21b3a34b2de9 at pin time
limitations: The pin records the repository state, not the deployed provider. A provider-side model swap or revision change would be invisible to these hashes; per-run observed model id is required.
context.ts is pinned only as an advisory dependency; a full lock must include it (and any future renderer the prompt imports).
No generated prompt is stored in this pin; prompt content depends on the arm's memory set and request text, which are corpus/pilot inputs.
